steps.u: Review this pull request that adds password reset by email. Focus on security.

steps.r: const token = Math.random().toString(36).slice(2); await db.reset.insert({email, token}); await mail.send(email, link(token)); return res.status(user ? 200 : 404)
const r = await db.reset.find({token}); if (!r) return 400; await users.setPassword(r.email, pw); // token not deleted, no expiry

steps.a: Findings: tokens come from Math.random, which is predictable, and are stored in plain text; they never expire and are not invalidated after use; the 404 for unknown emails lets an attacker enumerate accounts.

i.content:
Blocking: use crypto random tokens, store only a hash, expire after 30 minutes, single use, always return 200.
Non-blocking: rate limit the request endpoint; log without the token.

reference.summary: Reviewed a password reset pull request and found predictable Math.random tokens stored in plain text, no expiry or single use, and a 404 response that enables account enumeration; wrote up blocking and non-blocking comments.
facts: tokens from a predictable random source stored in plain text
no expiry and not invalidated after use
different response for unknown emails allows enumeration

decisions.choice: mark token generation, storage, expiry and the 404 response as blocking
decisions.reason: each lets an attacker take over or discover accounts
